pages.title: Introduction
pages.description: numera brings NumPy's n-dimensional arrays, ufuncs, linear algebra, FFT and random numbers to Node.js, backed by a native C++ core.

pages.title: Installation
pages.description: Install numera from npm. Prebuilt binaries for macOS and Linux, no compiler needed.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: A ten-minute tour of numera: create arrays, do math, reduce, index and solve.

pages.title: Coming from NumPy
pages.description: How NumPy code translates to numera: naming, keyword arguments, indexing and return values.

pages.title: Array basics
pages.description: Shape, dtype, strides, views and copies, and converting to and from JavaScript values.

pages.title: Data types
pages.description: The 14 numeric dtypes, NumPy type promotion, weak JS scalars, casting rules and 64-bit integers.

pages.title: Broadcasting
pages.description: How arrays of different shapes combine in element-wise operations.

pages.title: Indexing and slicing
pages.description: get, slice and set: integer, slice, ellipsis, newaxis, integer-array and boolean-mask indexing.

pages.title: Reductions and statistics
pages.description: sum, mean, std and friends with axis, keepdims, dtype, initial and where.

pages.title: Random numbers
pages.description: Generator and RandomState, with the same streams as NumPy for the same seed.

pages.title: Linear algebra and FFT
pages.description: np.linalg and np.fft, including batched inputs and complex results.

pages.title: Errors and floating-point
pages.description: Typed error classes, seterr and errstate.

pages.title: TypeScript
pages.description: Types exported by numera and how to use them.

pages.title: Performance and memory
pages.description: How numera runs, what is fast, what is not, and how native memory is released.
